    {
      "startEvent": 531,
      "endEvent": 534,
      "contextStartEvent": 478,
      "contextEndEvent": 582,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "then I'd be subjecting God's very essence to my reasoning.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "A treats providing a reason for God's particular nature as improperly subjecting God to human reasoning (E531–534), restricting the requested examination. This is an explicit protective move rather than a compact slogan. However, E539–544 allows unknown reasons, and E552–582 also offers an epistemic limitation and category-error analogies."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 547,
      "endEvent": 548,
      "contextStartEvent": 524,
      "contextEndEvent": 582,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "The reason he has the nature he has is because he has the nature that he has.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The repeated identity claim occupies the place of the requested explanation for this nature rather than another (E545–548). Earlier immutability explains persistence, not that selection. A subsequently admits he cannot explain it and develops a transcendence account (E552–582), so this particular affirmation does not clearly make every objection inadmissible."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 622,
      "endEvent": 645,
      "contextStartEvent": 583,
      "contextEndEvent": 674,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "I wouldn't do that because to me that would be idolatrous and blasphemous.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity", "shame"],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "A expressly declines the alternative-nature thought experiment because it would violate his religious commitments (E630–645), after acknowledging that a logical-impossibility answer would require defense (E622–629). That protects the premise from this diagnostic challenge. He distinguishes examining truth from redefining God at E665–674; the refusal remains an argument boundary, not a slogan."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 735,
      "endEvent": 737,
      "contextStartEvent": 710,
      "contextEndEvent": 768,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "Of course we're not. You're an atheist and I'm a Christian.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The identity contrast answers B's concern about mutual understanding without explaining why their identities entail misunderstanding (E734–737). It could substitute for addressing the distinction between dishonesty and logical inconsistency. However, A has just supplied a substantive account at E727–733, making a conversational aside plausible; no critic-defect rule is established."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 779,
      "endEvent": 787,
      "contextStartEvent": 750,
      "contextEndEvent": 837,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "we have sufficient wisdom and that we know enough things",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["ridicule"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "A denies the right and ability to judge God's morality, treating judgment as requiring sufficient wisdom about all actions (E779–787). This excludes the proposed assessment through a general human-capacity barrier. He supplies a reason rather than a slogan, and E825–837 explains the appeal to God's knowledge; the protective scope concerns judging God."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 940,
      "endEvent": 966,
      "contextStartEvent": 888,
      "contextEndEvent": 988,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "There is no possibility for us to reach up to the clouds and bring God down",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity"],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "A rules out judging divine morality because humans lack God's knowledge and attributes, categorizing their standards as subjective and their judgment as mistaken (E940–966). This shields divine conduct through a general disqualification of evaluators. It remains an articulated epistemic argument; E908–920 also qualifies omniscience as a possible factor rather than the moral standard itself."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1935,
      "endEvent": 1949,
      "contextStartEvent": 1918,
      "contextEndEvent": 1977,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "I absolutely do forfeit my right to judge God. I let him be God.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "no",
